109: ## Proposition fields
110: 
111: Every proposition has `id`, `kind`, the complete `statement`, `definitions`
112: (D IDs), `binders`, and `objects`:
113: 
114: - `binders`: `{symbol, type}` records for statement-bound variables. These do
115:   not introduce free variables in a consuming R. Register actual nested scope
116:   in the statement; alpha-rename to avoid global shadowing.
117: - `objects`: distinct names of mathematical objects actually used in the
118:   statement, from frozen parameters/primitives, referenced D closure or these
119:   binders. A D also has these fields for its defining expression.
120: 
121: These are inventories, not a parser-generated list. Audit A must find omitted
122: objects by reading actual prose/formulas. Export all formulas and conditions;
123: another N ID or an original equation number cannot replace their content.
124: 
125: | kind | ID | Producer | Additional fields |
126: |---|---|---|---|
127: | `hypothesis` | Hddd | none | exactly matches frozen H statement |
128: | `mathlib` | Mddd | none | `source` record below |
129: | `external` | Eddd | none | `source` record below |
130: | `internal` | Nddd | exactly one | `origin` locating source or explaining added bridge |
131: | `target` | P | exactly one | exact frozen `conclusion` |
132: 
133: A source record contains `statement` (exact NL restatement), `evidence` (file
134: hashes), and `hypotheses` (complete applicability obligations, not their proof).
135: M additionally has `declaration`, `module`, `mathlib_commit`, `source_path`,
136: `source_sha256`, `signature` (complete Lean output), and `declaration_kind` equal
137: to `theorem` or `proved_instance`. A definition/opaque constant is not a proved
138: source proposition. Library definitions belong in D. A named M's official
139: library dependencies need not be copied into the project graph; pin the library
140: and inspect relevant axioms. Do not introduce project results as library M.
141: M evidence includes the successful version-1 report from `probe_mathlib.py`,
142: with the same ID, declaration, full signature, source bytes and toolchain pins.
143: In the clean Yui NL0 carrier, `probe_library` produces this evidence and the
144: submission adapter binds exact signature/source metadata from the successful
145: probe matching the selected M ID and actual declaration selector. Those metadata
146: fields may be omitted from that tool's submitted JSON; canonical graph files
147: still contain them in full. No unprobed source is filled from model memory.
148: The clean probe resolves genuine aliases to their canonical kernel name and
149: discovers the actual defining module. A requested module is only a locator
150: hint; its correction is recorded, never silently treated as source evidence.
151: Native type printing (and the legacy `#check @declaration` probe) preserves the complete outer telescope,
152: including implicit/typeclass conditions, using ordinary notation for nested
153: structure applications. Recursive expansion of inherited structure arguments
154: is unnecessary; omitted hypotheses or ellipsis are not permitted. The actual
155: kernel declaration kind, axioms, source bytes and version pins remain evidence.
156: For a local development revision the same tool also accepts
157: `{base_input: "declared-task-ID.json", patches: [...]}` when that explicit frozen
158: task document contains `{spec, graph}`. Patches are JSON data operations
159: `add`, `remove`, `replace`, or `test`, each with an absolute JSON pointer inside
160: `/spec/...` or `/graph/...` and a `value` except for `remove`. Array append uses
161: `/-`. An additional `replace_text` operation has `path`, `old` and `new`
162: instead of `value`: it replaces exactly one nonempty literal occurrence inside
163: an existing string. Missing or ambiguous matches are rejected; this is not a
164: regular expression or executable code. It preserves the rest of a long proof
165: paragraph without asking the model to retype it.
166: Every submission starts from the immutable named input, not the previous
167: failed candidate. The controller records the base hash and actual edits, then
168: performs the identical full source/structure checks. Successful output is still
169: the complete canonical `{spec,graph}`. This is an authoring convenience for
170: unaccepted candidates, not an incremental Audit A receipt or permission to
171: modify accepted/frozen source during a translation run. Actual mathematical
172: changes still invalidate affected reviews.
173: Within the same authoring stage, an actual check also returns its
174: `candidate_number`. Use `{base_candidate: N, patches: [...]}` to revise that
175: exact checked draft, including a structurally rejected draft. `read_draft`
176: can inspect a narrow JSON pointer in that own draft. These are the model's
177: own prior submissions plus bound metadata, not other tasks or local files.
178: Every edit still undergoes the full checker, and no draft inherits acceptance.
179: Resubmit an exact own draft with `{accept_candidate: N}` after a successful
180: check. Once a same-stage draft exists, returning to `base_input` requires an
181: explicit `reset_base: true`; this deliberately discards accumulated edits.
182: Without that explicit reset, use `base_candidate` so a later bookkeeping fix
183: cannot silently discard earlier mathematical corrections.
184: The adapter does not rewrite mathematical statements, hypotheses, definitions,
185: binders or arguments. Their fidelity remains the author's and auditor's work.
186: The following two explicit serialization forms copy the author's declared
187: data; they do not infer mathematics or grant Audit A acceptance:
188: 
189: - An S `text`, D `definition`, or `spec.hypotheses[i].statement` may be `{from_task: "declared-input-ID", start_line: 10,
190:   end_line: 20}`. The controller copies exactly those inclusive lines of the
191:   already frozen same-stage input into an ordinary canonical string. It stores
192:   input/text hashes, the exact range and the canonical destination pointer.
193:   Only these proof/definition/hypothesis text fields have this form;
194:   undeclared files, other tasks and old candidates are not source IDs. Read the
195:   materialized draft, normalize source labels to legitimate input/F references,
196:   supply declarations/conditions and retain the complete argument. Copying the
197:   original proof does not establish closed-premise sufficiency. A copied
198:   definition still needs its complete declarations, dependencies and guards;
199:   it grants no mathematical property. A copied H must be a complete original
200:   GIVEN, with its origin retained; copying a desired conclusion or a claim
201:   from the proof does not make it a permissible hypothesis.
202: - `{base_candidate: N, source_uses: [{inference: "R001", at: "S001",
203:   input: "M001", bindings: "actual substitution", hypothesis_checks: [...]}]}`
204:   records existing M/E calls selected explicitly by the author. Each call adds
205:   its ID to that R's `inputs` and S's `uses`, and writes the supplied application
206:   record. Optional `id: Addd` distinguishes actual uses and is required for E.
207:   Exact replay is idempotent; a conflicting existing application must be
208:   explicitly patched. No new proposition/source or proof text is generated.
209:   Every normal check and actual Audit A still runs, including whether the
210:   theorem is actually used and each condition really follows from the packet.
211: 
212: To avoid retranscribing mandatory duplicate strings, its tool input may omit
213: an H node's `statement` (copied from the same artifact's `spec.hypotheses`),
214: P's `statement` (copied from `spec.conclusion`), or an E/M `source.statement`
215: (copied from that proposition's primary `statement`). This is serialization of
216: one authoritative text, not a second premise or an inferred theorem. Canonical
217: files contain all fields. Conflicting supplied duplicates are rejected with
218: both texts shown; they are never silently overwritten. The actual external
219: `source_statement` and the probed Lean signature remain separate source-fidelity
220: evidence that Audit A must compare to the primary project restatement.
221: Use a fresh probe output directory for a new source-query version. The helper
222: refuses to overwrite existing evidence; `--replace-existing` deliberately
223: archives previous outputs and revokes the old active receipt before rerunning.
224: The checker verifies this record binding; it does not authenticate a fabricated
225: execution transcript. Audit A still reads the actual source and checks meaning.
226: 
227: E additionally has nonempty strings `author`, `title`, `version`, `identifier`,
228: `locator`, `notation_map`, `errata`, `source_kind`, `origin`, `retrieved_at`,
229: `source_statement`, `context`, `qualification`, and `version_check`, plus
230: `primary_evidence`: a nonempty list of hashed evidence records also present in
231: `evidence`. `source_statement` records the actual source theorem and its full
232: conditions, separately from the project's restatement. `version_check` states
233: the check date, scope, findings and effect; `qualification` explains source
234: category and proved-result eligibility. Read the full
235: [external-theorem review standard](external-theorems.md).
236: The explicit [conditional-source route](conditional-sources.md) additionally
237: allows `verification: {status: "UNVERIFIED_PRIMARY", record: {path, sha256}}`.
238: Only with that validated record may `primary_evidence` be empty. The record
239: binds the exact complete secondary statement and actual failed retrievals;
240: Audit A remains source-unverified and the final workflow stays conditional.
241: A DOI/URL alone is insufficient. Include an
242: accessible local primary document and precise excerpt/location evidence. Do not call
243: the target work's unproved internal lemma an imported E. Existing internally
244: proved modules need a separate expanded graph or a versioned proof handoff;
245: version 2 does not silently certify an opaque module.
246: 
247: Every retained non-H proposition must be in P's backward dependency closure.
248: Every frozen H is present as an initial graph node, including an unused H.
249: Report unused H rather than removing it or changing the original statement.

1: # Self-containment details
2: 
3: This details the statement/object and dependency/scope requirements grouped
4: under Audit A's statement_closure and dependency_closure criteria. The
5: [shared Audit A section](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
6: is the acceptance authority for author and auditor; this annex supplies
7: interpretation and examples, not an independent permission policy.
8: 
9: ## Two boundaries
10: 
11: Accepted NL0 is a complete proof relative to its declared H/E/M roots, frozen
12: logical foundation and version-bound mathematically reviewed background notes. It is not an outline requiring the original manuscript to
13: recover missing definitions, formulas, assumptions, or arguments. E/M statements
14: are fully restated; their primary sources are inspected for provenance, not
15: used to supply unstated premises. The fixed library's own proof dependencies
16: need not be recopied. The target work's internal results must be proved here.
17: 
18: Every R must also be checkable from its packet alone: the complete statements
19: of its direct inputs, their required definitions/declarations, its complete
20: output, its local declarations, and its own argument. Another R's proof body,
21: an ancestor not listed as an input, an ambient original H, an original-source
22: crosswalk, or remembered material is not an additional mathematical resource.
23: Whole-target/source-fidelity checks are separate from this local proof check.
24: Under mathematical-background-v2-1, a reviewer may positively assess routine
25: local mathematical facts and record precise statements, available conditions
26: and justification. Exact Mathlib bindings are deferred to nl02lean; no native
27: query is required for ordinary background. These notes add neither H nor a
28: core proof route. Mathematical uncertainty still blocks. See
29: [background notes](background-notes.md).
30: 
31: Original theorem conditions are H nodes, including conditions that could be
32: encoded in a refined type. Parameters introduce ambient data/structures, not
33: an ambient stock of original hypotheses. For example, declare a vector and
34: put its required nonzero condition in H; do not write “nonzero vector” in its
35: parameter type and use that condition from an empty input list. The same rule
36: applies to characteristic/range conditions and equations. An R must list every
37: original H it actually uses. Standard structure operations/axioms and the fixed
38: finite-language rules remain available; no new substantive theorem is added.
39: 
40: An output must be understandable and callable without reading its producer's
41: argument. Include the actual equalities/inequalities, binder types, hypotheses,
42: parameter windows, constant dependencies, representatives and a.e./pointwise
43: meaning. Global defined notation can be expanded from the packet. A formula
44: number, theorem name, or paragraph location cannot replace mathematical content.
45: Source locators belong in provenance fields. New mathematical prose uses direct
46: input IDs and previously proved local F IDs, not inherited numbered references.
47: 
48: ## Object closure
49: 
50: For every mathematical object actually appearing in a statement, definition,
51: local declaration, or proof, locate one legitimate declaration:
52: 
53: 1. A frozen parameter, explicit logical primitive, or global D definition.
54:    State its meaning, type/domain and parameter dependence. Global primitives
55:    cover only core typed syntax, not a dictionary of subject-specific objects.
56:    New subjects use the same parameter/definition/local declaration mechanism;
57:    symbol registration never licenses a theorem.
58: 2. A binder inside the current proposition's full statement. Its scope remains
59:    that statement. A variable bound in an input does not become a free object
60:    in the consuming proof; instantiate the statement explicitly.
61: 3. A local declaration before first use, recording its kind, type, exact
62:    declaration, introduction basis, and scope. An arbitrary variable requires
63:    legitimate quantifier introduction; a definition uses already available
64:    objects; a witness requires an input or an earlier local existence proof.
65: 
66: A declaration cannot grant existence, uniqueness, invertibility, regularity,
67: or a desired property merely by naming an object. Those obligations require
68: proof. Any D guard needed to use the object must be a direct R input, not a
69: theorem silently recovered from ancestor closure. Record mutually compatible
70: choices and witness dependence. Temporary assumptions stay inside R and must
71: be correctly discharged. Branch witnesses, local facts and local notation
72: cannot escape their scopes. Export a quantified or conditional statement when
73: needed, rather than a free private name. Global names are reserved; dummy
74: variables may be reused in disjoint local scopes.
75: 
76: ## Dependency closure
77: 
78: Inventory actual factual uses from the prose back to their grounds, not just
79: from an input list forward to a generic `uses` list. Each substantive imported theorem, prior project lemma or original
80: assumption must be a direct input. Eligible routine mathematical facts are recorded as mathematical audit notes
81: with actual local grounds, without requiring a native implementation lookup. A definition supplies meaning, not a theorem. An R output is not its
82: own premise. Adding the desired formula as an unproved input is not a repair.
83: 
84: Explicit local calculations and fully proved intermediate facts may remain
85: inside R. Give a reused local fact a full F statement and identify its earlier
86: derivation and open assumptions. No separate graph vertex is needed for every
87: algebraic equality. A nontrivial imported result cannot be called a local
88: calculation. Substantive reusable lemmas should become N/R pairs; any fact
89: reused by another R must be exported in a complete proposition statement.
90: 
91: The controller owns `spec.logic.calculations` and the small core syntax table
92: (`nl0/scripts/foundations.py`). The clean author tool binds omitted metadata and
93: rejects extra author permissions or task-specific primitives. This fixed
94: language grants no MVT, FTC, Fubini, convergence, compactness or regularity
95: theorem. Such facts need legitimate explicit inputs, an actual local derivation or
96: eligible positively reviewed mathematical background; the syntax table alone
97: grants none of them.
98: An author-written permission claim, in any field or prose, has no authority.
99: Ordinary typed arithmetic notation is part of this fixed language: natural
100: numbers, integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers mean their standard
101: structures with usual numerals and operations. Finite calculations include
102: their zero/one laws, such as `a+0=a`, as well as explicit algebra/order
103: derivations. Do not demand a separate E/M for an operation token or an allowed
104: finite calculation. This does not grant calculus, topology or measure theorems.
105: Conversely, inspect an actual displayed local derivation before demanding a
106: duplicate E/M input for its conclusion. A named consequence proved by permitted
107: finite algebra/order steps is not an imported premise. If a local derivation
108: fails, locate its unsupported implication rather than its absent theorem name.
109: 
110: Metadata accounts for the argument but never replaces it. Copying all inputs
111: into a single `uses` record, registering a symbol without declaring it in the
112: proof, or writing a PASS label cannot establish closure.
113: 
114: ## Operational acceptance
115: 
116: 1. Author using the node template. Reverse-check the actual prose for missing
117:    declarations, unexpanded references and unlisted facts before freezing.
118: 2. Generate a packet for each R. The v2 generator supplies no original proof,
119:    producer proofs, provenance file locators, extra ancestor statements or
120:    undeclared ambient H. Direct source contracts and required definitions are
121:    included. Packet hashes bind the mathematical input actually reviewed.
122: 3. Review all closure/inference checks, admitting positively checked routine
123:    background notes under the shared policy. Record concrete packet locations and reasons for every verdict.
124: 4. Perform a fresh local mathematical replay. The reviewer gets the skill instructions
125:    and that packet, without original proof,
126:    other R bodies, author review
127:    notes, old verdicts, or an answer key. Record the actual carrier, packet hash,
128:    prior exposure and mathematical material read. Skill instructions supply no
129:    extra mathematical premise. Do not falsely claim a same-context rereading
130:    is a fresh replay. This rule does not authorize starting a new external
131:    service or agent; if the required carrier has not been used, keep replay
132:    UNVERIFIED and report that limit.
133:    Prior exposure means known task/proof material supplied or read in earlier
134:    contexts; this is not a claim about unknown pretraining contents. Learned
135:    mathematical knowledge cannot replace a missing declared premise or proof.
136: 5. An ineligible missing declaration, missing statement content, unlisted substantive theorem or need
137:    to look outside the packet blocks acceptance. Record the defect; do not
138:    silently repair it while assigning PASS. Return substantive/structural defects to authoring and review the frozen
139:    revision; eligible background notes need no author rewrite. Routine completion does not require a
140:    separate user interruption for every omission. Distinguish a representation
141:    defect from a substantive mathematical gap under the existing gap policy.
142: 
143: The code rejects explicit malformed references, inventories, scopes, guards
144: and receipts. It does not infer hidden hypotheses from property words in types,
145: or decide theorem applications by matching a list of mathematical names.
146: These semantic obligations apply equally to every subject and remain part of
147: author inspection and Audit A. An omitted inventory entry or unnamed
148: theorem hidden in prose still requires actual semantic review. Freshness and
149: truthful reviewer identity need execution evidence; record shape/hashes cannot
150: authenticate them. No natural-language audit is a Lean kernel certificate.

251: ## Inference fields
252: 
253: Required fields: `id: Rddd`, `inputs` (unique proposition IDs), `output` (one
254: N/P ID), `definitions` (direct D references), `rules` (permitted logic-rule
255: names), `locals`, `argument`, and `applications`.
256: 
257: - `locals`: `{symbol, type, scope}` records. Scope identifies a binding inside
258:   this inference; names cannot shadow globals. Two bindings in different
259:   scopes/nodes may use the same spelling. Bound variables of source theorems
260:   can be alpha-renamed and instantiated. Audit actual binding/freshness.
261:   In v2 also require `start`, `end` (inclusive S IDs), `kind` (`arbitrary`,
262:   `definition`, or `witness`), `declaration` (full introduction), `from_inputs`,
263:   `from_local` (prior F IDs) and `objects` (already available objects used to
264:   introduce this one). A witness must have an input/local existence basis.
265:   The checker verifies declared availability/order, not the existence claim's
266:   semantics. Source-bound variables need a legitimate local instantiation.
267:   The `scope` label and inclusive start/end must agree with the prose. Keep an
268:   object live through its last actual use. Establish an existence F in an
269:   earlier S, then choose its witness in a subsequent S; using a newly produced
270:   F as the witness basis in the same paragraph is a forward reference.
271: - `argument`: ordered records `{id: Sddd, text, uses, uses_local, objects,
272:   produces, introduces, discharges}`. S IDs are inference-local and unique. `uses`
273:   lists direct graph inputs used at this point. Local facts established earlier
274:   in the prose do not become graph inputs. The union of `uses` must equal
275:   `inputs`. A citation's presence is not semantic evidence that it was used.
276:   `uses_local` lists only earlier F IDs; `objects` lists the actually used
277:   global/active local objects. `produces` holds complete local facts
278:   `{id: Fddd, statement, binders, objects, assumptions}`; assumptions lists remaining
279:   local L IDs on which the fact depends. A local fact cannot be used before
280:   its production or outside its assumption/object scope. A paragraph cannot
281:   cite its newly produced F as a previous premise. Formulas to be reused by a
282:   different R must appear in the exported proposition, not only in `produces`.
283: - `introduces`/`discharges`: lists of inference-local assumption IDs (e.g.
284:   `L1`). Temporary assumptions are never proposition vertices. Every introduced
285:   ID is unique in this inference and must be discharged once, no earlier than
286:   introduction. These lists account for prose; Audit A checks the actual
287:   formula, scope, and chosen rule. A correctly closed implication may retain
288:   the assumption in its antecedent. Deleting the ID cannot justify an output.
289: - `applications`: records covering every directly used E/M input, with
290:   `{input, at: Sddd, bindings, hypothesis_checks}`.
291:   `bindings` is a nonempty string spelling out the actual variable/parameter
292:   substitution; it is not a JSON mapping. `hypothesis_checks` is an ordered
293:   list of nonempty strings, one per declared source obligation. For example,
294:   `"bindings": "Set the source parameter a to the current x."` records a
295:   substitution; it does not prove its conditions.
296:   The S paragraph must list
297:   this input in `uses`; only local facts available before that paragraph may
298:   supply application conditions. E applications additionally require
299:   an inference-local unique `id: Addd`; different actual uses of the same E
300:   need separate IDs and records. M may also use explicit A IDs for repeated
301:   instances; a legacy M without `id` uses its input ID as the unique key.
302:   `hypothesis_checks` has one nonempty
303:   explanation for each corresponding source obligation. A hypothesis needs an
304:   actual argument from inputs/H/local proved facts; filling a string is only
305:   an accounting check. Prove substantive normalization bridges as N nodes.
306: 
307: Input-free R nodes are permitted only for explicitly shown calculations or
308: logical/definitional consequences. They are audited proofs, not a fourth kind
309: of trusted source. Transitive inputs need not be repeated unless used directly.
310: 
311: ## Audit record
312: 
313: `audit-a.json` contains `format_version`, `graph_sha256`, `spec_sha256`,
314: `reviewer` (`identity`, `mode`, `independent`, `disclosure`), `target_review`,
315: `definition_reviews`, `source_reviews`, and `inference_reviews`.
316: 
317: Each review contains `verdict: PASS|FAIL|UNVERIFIED`, substantive `notes`, and
318: hashed `evidence`. Yui inference reviews contain five grouped check review objects:
319: `statement_closure`, `dependency_closure`, `argument`, `applicability`,
320: `packet_replay`. Object scope and exact output correctness remain required
321: inside these grouped mathematical assessments.
322: Each check has `{verdict, notes, evidence, locations}`. `locations` contains
323: JSON pointers resolving inside that R's actual packet, such as
324: `/inputs/0/statement` or `/inference/argument/1/text`. PASS requires at least
325: one actual inspected location; a boolean/enum alone is insufficient.
326: Every D, every E/M source, every R, and the target must be covered exactly once.
327: Spec input hashes and source evidence are read back; malformed/duplicate JSON
328: keys, missing files, changed bytes, failed verdicts, and stale audit hashes fail.
329: 
330: Use audit `format_version: 4` for all new Yui records. A detailed-NL0 audit v3
331: cannot establish format-4 acceptance. Historical audit v1/v2 remains inspectable only
332: with historical graph v1 and --legacy, never as current acceptance.
333: Each E source review additionally has `citation_checks`, mapping exactly
334: `literature_identity`, `result_location`, `statement_fidelity`,
335: `context_completeness`, `version_and_eligibility` to separate ordinary review
336: objects `{verdict, notes, evidence}`.
337: Each version-4 inference review additionally has `external_applications`,
338: mapping exactly its E application A IDs to records
339: `{input, verdict, notes, evidence, bindings_review, hypothesis_reviews,
340: conclusion_review, bridges}`. `input` must match A's E; each nested review
341: has `{verdict, notes, evidence}`; the ordered `hypothesis_reviews` list matches
342: all source obligations one for one. `bridges` lists N nodes already in R's
343: direct input list. A bridge string is not a proof of that bridge.
344: 
345: Each inference review also has `replay: {packet_sha256, mode, carrier,
346: prior_exposure, read_materials}`. Modes are `unperformed`,
347: `same_context_diagnostic`, and `fresh_packet_only`. A passing replay/overall
348: inference requires the actual fresh carrier, empty prior proof exposure, and
349: `read_materials` equal to `["packet:<hash>"]` for mathematical input. Skill
350: instructions supply the procedure, not additional mathematics. The hash must
351: match the regenerated packet. Keep traces as evidence; metadata cannot
352: authenticate a claimed identity or prove truthful isolation.
353: 
354: Format 4 may additionally bind `review_trace:{path,sha256}` for actual tool logs.
355: This is execution metadata, not a native theorem source or an extra premise.
356: `library_evidence` contains only the successful pinned evidence of explicitly
357: retained native mathlib notes; ordinary mathematical notes require none.
358: 
359: `audit-template` creates only UNVERIFIED reviews, empty check locations and an
360: unperformed replay. It refuses to overwrite an existing output. It does not
361: inherit author notes or old verdicts. `inspect-audit` can inspect this pending
362: record; `check --audit` rejects it. Each PASS must come from actual review.
363: 
364: `check --audit` accepts only fully passing records. `inspect-audit --audit`
365: also validates the completeness and evidence of FAIL/UNVERIFIED records and
366: returns their unresolved review paths; success of inspection is not proof
367: acceptance. Overall PASS with a failed child review never passes acceptance.
368: 
369: Mode `same_context_self_audit` requires `independent: false`. If claiming an
370: independent review, disclose its actual carrier and input boundary; this file
371: does not authenticate identity or prove independence.
372: 
373: ## Local packet
374: 
375: The v2 packet contains `contract_version`, `case_id`, spec/graph hashes,
376: parameters, fixed logic, pins, expanded definitions, complete input/output
377: ports, the current inference, a warning, and `packet_sha256`. Source ports keep
378: applicability obligations and M signatures; primary-document verification is
379: separate. Producer arguments, original-proof locations, source proof text,
380: non-input H and extra ancestor/guard statements are not supplied. Guards must
381: already be direct inputs. The packet intentionally omits the global full target
382: so that its unstated premises cannot become an ambient local hypothesis.
383: 
384: Its digest is SHA256 of UTF-8 canonical JSON (`sort_keys=True`,
385: `ensure_ascii=False`, `separators=(",", ":")`) excluding `packet_sha256`.
386: It is independent of audit-verdict fields, avoiding a circular receipt hash.
387: Packets are generated views and never a second editable proof authority.
388: 
389: ## Mechanical boundaries
390: 
391: The checker validates declared objects, the frozen contract, graph closure,
392: notation-name metadata, citation parity, local-assumption accounting, guarded
393: definition availability, and hash-bound audit coverage. It verifies source
394: checkout/file hashes, not the truth of a source restatement. The printed
395: signature must be obtained from a successful pinned Lean probe and compared by
396: the auditor; an arbitrary string called `signature` is not verification.
397: 
398: The checker cannot establish that a natural-language formula is well typed,
399: that two spellings have the same mathematical meaning, that a hidden theorem
400: was not used, that a local witness did not escape the prose, or that an argument
401: is valid. Those are explicit Audit A obligations. Neither a JSON PASS nor a
402: fabricated complete audit receipt is a mathematical certificate.
403: Numbered-reference diagnostics reject common opaque references, not every
404: possible paraphrase or hidden import. Behavioral tests must actually ask an
405: auditor to review unseen controls; manually prefilled FAIL records only test
406: receipt rejection and must be reported as such.
407: 
408: ## Mathematical background receipt extension
409: 
410: New receipts declare `background_policy: "mathematical-background-v2-1"`.
411: Each R may contain background_notes with precise mathematics, local grounds and
412: actual justification; native lookup is not required. A new supplemented replay
413: uses fresh_packet_with_mathematical_background. Optional existing native notes
414: retain their complete bound library evidence; mathematical/elementary notes
415: carry no native source claim. The authored graph remains unchanged. Other
416: variant consumers must reject unsupported receipts instead of dropping fields.
417: 
418: `nl0.validate` returns the note supplement/hash and note count. A packet read
419: from an accepted source includes its notes and the original reviewed-packet
420: hash. This enriched view is not claimed to be the original replay input.
421: Translation binds the supplement in `contract.source.background_supplement_sha256`.
422: 
423: The interface source also retains the complete `background_supplement`, not
424: just its hash. Plan steps list the relevant qualified note IDs, for example
425: `background_notes:["R004.BG001"]`. Workflow freeze checks the paragraph mapping;
426: local Lean packets receive only their selected notes.

1: # Package local reasoning as true theorem nodes
2: 
3: The main graph has only E/M/H source propositions. A temporary assumption is
4: an argument-local device, never a trusted graph vertex. Every exported N/P is
5: a complete claim under the frozen original context. The audit inspects the
6: local derivation; surface implication syntax alone is insufficient.
7: The complete [neutral JSON example](../templates/quantified-implication-example.md)
8: shows an arbitrary binder, a local antecedent, its discharge and the full
9: quantified output. Follow this accounting rather than silently granting a
10: property in a local object's type.
11: 
12: ## Implication and contradiction
13: 
14: To prove `X -> Y`, introduce X inside one argument, derive Y from the declared
15: inputs, then discharge X into the antecedent. Output `X -> Y`, not Y. To use Y
16: unconditionally later, supply an actually proved X and apply implication
17: elimination. A local X and a proved X are not the same proof object.
18: 
19: To prove `not X`, derive false under local X and discharge X by negation
20: introduction. To prove P by classical contradiction, first produce the complete
21: theorem `not P -> false` (equivalently `not not P`), then apply the fixed
22: classical rule. A single R may combine the operations if every local assumption
23: is accounted for. No classical double-negation elimination under an
24: intuitionistic-only policy.
25: 
26: Example graph: N1 `(not P -> Q)`, N2 `not Q`, R1 outputs N3
27: `(not P -> false)`, R2 outputs P. The argument of R1 locally assumes not P,
28: applies N1 and N2, and closes that assumption. No `not P` root is added.
29: The fallacy “assume P, obtain P, discharge and output P” fails: its valid output
30: would be `P -> P`.
31: 
32: ## Cases
33: 
34: From an already proved `A or B or C`, obtain a common target Q by complete
35: conditional lemmas `A -> Q`, `B -> Q`, `C -> Q`, then disjunction elimination.
36: Alternatively prove `not A`, `not B` and conclude C using the original
37: disjunction. Eliminating A/B without a proved exhaustive disjunction cannot
38: establish C. A branch producing false can produce the common target by false
39: elimination; it does not make false an unconditional source proposition.
40: 
41: Proof bodies may contain all branches locally instead of exporting every
42: branch lemma. Check coverage, identical target/ambient context, and the absence
43: of sibling-branch fact/witness leakage. Introduce/discharge each branch-local
44: assumption in its actual scope.
45: 
46: ## Quantifiers, witnesses, and induction
47: 
48: For universal introduction use an arbitrary variable, then close its binder.
49: It must not occur free in an undischarged extra assumption. If the intended
50: theorem has a premise H(x), retain it in the quantified implication.
51: 
52: For existential elimination start from a proved existence statement, choose a
53: fresh local witness with exactly its stated properties, and prove a conclusion
54: independent of that witness's private identity. A witness depending on n does
55: not yield one witness valid for every n. Do not turn a local witness into a
56: globally available constant without a legitimate, recorded construction.
57: 
58: For natural-number induction prove the base and the complete step
59: `forall n, Q(n) -> Q(n+1)` and use induction to conclude `forall n, Q(n)`.
60: The induction hypothesis is local to the step; there is no circular graph edge.
61: If the step invokes the hypothesis at a transformed point s, include
62: `forall s` in the induction invariant. Well-founded induction needs the exact
63: well-founded relation/decrease justification; the word “induct” is not enough.
64: 
65: ## Local notation
66: 
67: Global symbols are reserved. Local binders can repeat across separate nodes
68: or separate binding scopes in a node, but cannot shadow a global symbol.
69: `sum_{k=1}^N` binds k only in that expression. Source theorem dummy variables
70: are alpha-renamed locally, not registered as a new global object each time.
71: Freshness, witness dependencies, constant uniformity, and binder scope are
72: mathematical audit obligations; a list of names does not verify the formula.
73: In v2, local declarations identify introduction kind/basis and inclusive S
74: start/end positions. An input-bound name needs instantiation; a witness needs
75: an actual existence premise. Local F facts record their complete statement,
76: statement-local binders, used objects and remaining assumptions. Neither a
77: fact nor a chosen witness may escape its scope. The checker accounts for
78: declared scopes; Audit A must also inspect the actual quantifier reasoning.

1: # NL0 construction and tool template
2: 
3: Use [Audit A's shared criteria](../references/audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
4: as the mathematical authority. This template explains data/tool construction;
5: it is not a parallel acceptance policy. Read the [schema](../references/nl0-format.md),
6: [construction guide](../references/nl0-authoring.md), and the complete neutral
7: [submission](submission-example.md), [source application](source-application-example.md)
8: and [quantified implication](quantified-implication-example.md) examples.
9: These examples show format and derivations, not certified benchmark answers.
10: 
11: The complete [guarded-definition example](guarded-definition-example.md) shows
12: how to organize a target that includes an object's existence and a property
13: of that object. For a real a let Q(r) mean r=a. R001 first proves N001, unique
14: existence of a Q witness, without using w. D002 then defines w as that unique
15: witness with requires=[N001]. R002 takes N001 as a direct input and proves the
16: full target: unique existence and w=a. Listing D002 in the global spec does
17: not let R001 use it before its guard. Do not hide an unproved guard in a
18: restricted domain when the frozen target requires a statement on the full
19: original domain. This pattern adds no new assumption or mathematical source.
20: 
21: ## Construct one coherent candidate
22: 
23: 1. For `target` and `definitions`, extract the original H, ambient parameters
24:    and global typed definitions. Preserve the original source locations. Do
25:    not change a parameter's mathematical kind while fixing its metadata.
26: 2. For `statement_closure`, design N/R interfaces from what their
27:    consumers actually need. Put the complete formulas, quantified conditions
28:    and space identifications into the exported statement, not only its body.
29: 3. For `dependency_closure` and `argument`, construct
30:    each proof unit alongside its premises. List exact source inputs or display
31:    a prior local derivation for every substantive fact beyond the fixed
32:    calculations. Split when local context changes; avoid a giant S whose
33:    changing objects must later be repaired one at a time.
34: 4. For `sources` and `applicability`, inspect each selected native/primary
35:    source, preserve its complete contract and ground each instantiated premise.
36:    A signature lookup or a sentence claiming a hypothesis is true is not proof
37:    of that hypothesis. Reuse an adequate proved source rather than re-proving
38:    it; a project-specific bridge still requires its displayed derivation.
39: 5. For object declarations and local scopes under dependency_closure, introduce objects and conditional premises
40:    at their actual first use. Keep witness bases and local F dependencies
41:    correct. Preserve exact coefficients and ranges when copying calculations.
42: 6. Run check_draft, correct its actual located records, inspect every own
43:    conditional packet, and report readiness below. The independent auditor
44:    applies the same criteria after definitive submission.
45: 
46: ## Canonical data shapes
47: 
48: Submit {spec,graph} using the schema, or preserve an own draft with
49: {base_candidate:N,patches:[...]}. The controller binds identity, input/pin
50: hashes, fixed language and exact native metadata; it does not rewrite proof
51: content. Use read_draft with a narrow pointer after an edit rejection.
52: Unique existing @ID/@symbol selectors work for own-stage reads/patches;
53: inserting array elements still uses numeric indices or /-. Audit evidence
54: uses standard JSON pointers instead of this selector extension.
55: 
56: For multiline changes prefer read_draft(candidate=N,pointer="/graph/inferences/@R001/argument/@S001/text",
57: start_line=1,end_line=20). It returns the actual numbered lines, total_lines
58: and complete text_sha256. Use an edit with exactly
59: {op:"replace_lines",path:"/graph/inferences/@R001/argument/@S001/text",start_line:4,end_line:5,
60: text:"replacement including its intended line endings",text_sha256:"the returned hash"}.
61: Ranges are positive and inclusive. Unselected text and line endings are
62: preserved; stale hashes are rejected. Include a line terminator when a
63: nonempty replacement precedes retained lines. Empty text deletes the range.
64: All ordinary validation and later Audit A still apply.
65: For reads only, an end beyond the string returns its remaining existing lines
66: and the actual range; the start must exist and at most 250 lines may be
67: requested. Line edits still reject any out-of-range end and never clamp it.
68: 
69: Each D has type, full definition, binders, used objects, D dependencies and
70: proved guards. Each H/E/M/N/P has full statement, definitions, binders, objects
71: and appropriate source/origin fields. Each R has direct inputs, one output,
72: definitions, rules, locals, argument and real source applications. Each S has
73: actual text, uses, earlier uses_local, objects, complete produces F statements,
74: and assumption introductions/discharges. Each source application has input,
75: at:Sddd, bindings and actual hypothesis_checks. See the linked schema/examples
76: for exact names. source_uses can serialize one already selected M/E into the
77: R.inputs, S.uses and application together; supply the actual mathematical
78: bindings and grounds yourself.
79: 
80: When a declared frozen task already supplies a complete adequate definition,
81: D.definition may be {from_task:"input ID",start_line:N,end_line:M}, just like
82: S.text. The same form is available for spec.hypotheses[i].statement when the
83: selected passage states a complete original GIVEN. Keep its origin; never
84: promote a desired conclusion or proof claim to H. An H referring to the
85: target/problem for its missing content is not standalone.
86: The controller copies those exact lines to an ordinary canonical
87: string and records their hashes; it does not select or correct the definition.
88: Still declare its objects, binders, dependencies and guards. Normalize any
89: needed notation explicitly and preserve the supplied meaning. Copying never
90: grants a property or a mathematical PASS.
91: 
92: A local declaration has symbol, type, scope, start/end, kind, declaration,
93: from_inputs, from_local and objects. from_local holds earlier F proof IDs;
94: ordinary object dependencies belong in objects. A fact proved later in this
95: same paragraph is not yet a premise for choosing its witness. State it in an
96: earlier S. In sum_{k=0}^m a(k), k is expression-bound; the free objects are a,m.
97: A k used outside the sum needs its own declaration. Statement binders are
98: recorded with that statement; a variable spanning S paragraphs uses locals.
99: Changing a ledger entry does not rename an existing formula.
100: 
101: ## Actual own-packet inspection and release
102: 
103: After structural validation call read_author_packet(candidate,inference) for
104: every R. The returned view contains the real direct input/output statements,
105: definitions, logic and own proof, plus the shared contract binding. Read the
106: output without remembering its producer body. For each factual invocation,
107: identify its actual input or previous derivation. Complete closing notes use
108: these existing evidence groups; their criterion IDs are supplied by the
109: controller from Audit A. Cite actual H/M/E/N/F/R/S or candidate locations in
110: those notes; generic assurances are insufficient.
111: 
112: record_author_checks has this exact tool form (one row per actual N/P and R):
113: 
114: ```json
115: {
116:   "candidate": 7,
117:   "readiness": "no_known_issue",
118:   "open_issues": [],
119:   "resolutions": [],
120:   "original_context_note": "Located comparison of original target/H, definitions, selected source contracts and graph closure.",
121:   "output_notes": [{"id": "P", "note": "Located check of the full output and the derivation of every clause."}],
122:   "inference_notes": [{
123:     "id": "R001",
124:     "dependency_and_local_assumption_check": "Actual factual grounds, calculation, compatible inputs and discharged assumptions, with locations.",
125:     "source_application_check": "Actual substitutions and grounds for every source premise, or why no source is used.",
126:     "declaration_check": "Actual object introductions, types, witness bases and scopes, with locations."
127:   }]
128: }
129: ```
130: 
131: These are author claims, not PASS verdicts. If an obligation is unfinished,
132: set readiness=unresolved and list an issue such as
133: {id:"I001",criterion:"dependency_closure",location:"/graph/inferences/0/argument/0/text",note:"The exact missing input/derivation."}.
134: Use not_checked for unperformed inspection; incomplete notes can be saved,
135: but cannot release the artifact. Known issues persist across candidate edits.
136: Once corrected, provide resolutions:[{id:"I001",location:"/graph/inferences/0/argument/0/text",note:"The actual correction or justified withdrawal and its grounds."}].
137: Both issue and resolution locations must exist in the current candidate.
138: The context note checks the actual definition types and their prior guards;
139: inference notes check the exact source conclusion and any needed change of
140: domain or representation, rather than listing source names alone.
141: An empty new list cannot silently erase an old issue. The program checks
142: coverage, explicit state, locations and content/authority binding; mathematical
143: soundness still needs independent Audit A.
144: 
145: An actual own-packet read remains credited after an unrelated candidate edit
146: only when its complete displayed mathematical view and acceptance authority
147: have identical canonical contents. The recorded hash covers parameters, logic, selected
148: definitions, actual direct inputs/source contracts, output and full argument.
149: Changed views require new actual reads. Current whole-candidate release notes
150: are still invalidated by every edit, and known issues still need resolutions.
151: These are same-author read receipts, never inherited mathematical verdicts.
152: 
153: Only author_release_ready allows complete-artifact submission. Otherwise
154: continue the actual local proof/source work in this same stage. At a real
155: budget limit preserve the draft as unfinished. Normal completion difficulties
156: are not a substantive mathematical-gap report. Source/graph edits invalidate
157: bound closing notes. When ready, resubmit the exact candidate. Fresh Audit A
158: receives none of these notes or historical feedback.
159: 
160: ## Library access
161: 
162: find_library_sources offers a small verified pinned metadata index, not a
163: whitelist. An exact canonical name selects that declaration; ordinary terms
164: return ranked candidates with actual matched terms. Overlap does not establish
165: applicability. probe_library resolves genuine aliases and the actual module;
166: its optional module argument is only a locator hint. Read the pinned source
167: and compare its whole native signature with its NL restatement and actual
168: application. Predicates/data definitions are not source theorems. Same-stage
169: M-label renumbering can reuse exact metadata through a disclosed mapping;
170: it does not rewrite any mathematical statement or applicability argument.
171: 
172: ## Background granularity
173: 
174: Follow Audit A's shared verified-background admission rule. Register the main
175: tools; write ordinary rigorous mathematics rather than anticipating every
176: small Lean lemma. Correct elementary compression is allowed. Audit A can
177: verify an omitted routine library fact and attach a note without an author
178: rewrite. Missing original H, source uncertainty and substantive proof gaps
179: remain blocking. These audit notes later accompany each Lean task.

4: ## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements
5: 
6: Contract version: `yui-nl0-audit-a-2`.
7: 
8: The author and independent auditor use this same mathematical standard. NL0
9: reviews a complete natural-language proof and necessary mathematical detail.
10: Specific Lean declarations, signatures, representations and proof tactics are
11: implementation work for nl02lean, not prerequisites for ordinary NL0 review.
12: The following grouped criteria replace V1's ten separate per-R report rows.
13: 
14: | ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |

16: | `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the complete original theorem, every original H, quantifier, domain, normalization and supplied core proof route. A parameter or definition cannot hide a hypothesis or desired conclusion. |
17: | `definitions` | package | declaration_check | Define mathematical objects and notation sufficiently for their actual uses. Check types, dependencies, construction guards and legitimate local introductions. A definition grants no unproved property. |
18: | `sources` | package | original_context_note | Check complete E statements, primary-source identity, context and conditions under the source policy. An explicitly selected native M retains its bound signature checks; authors need not introduce M nodes for ordinary mathematical background. Unavailable originals remain disclosed UNVERIFIED source assumptions. |

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in

compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary positive real exponent s.

argument.text: Fix m, A and s as declared. Apply M001 to the Euclidean metric space R^m, its Borel measurable structure, exponent s and set A. At each finite positive scale, the formula's covers are exactly the covers in D002: a countable family can be enumerated by natural numbers, padding with empty sets if finite, and conversely a sequence is countable. All nonempty sets allowed at such a scale are bounded, so their extended diameters equal their ordinary finite Euclidean diameters. Empty members have cost zero in both definitions; since s>0, nonempty singletons also have zero cost. Thus the inner infimum is exactly the supplied scale content. The extra scale infinity in M001 adds nothing to the supremum: its admissible covers include all covers at scale 1, so its infimum is at most the scale-1 content. The finite positive extended scales are precisely the positive real scales. Taking their supremum proves F001: H^s(A)=μH[s](A). No dimensional normalization constant is introduced.

produces.statement: H^s(A)=μH[s](A).

argument.text: Use F001 to transport the four critical-exponent facts. Under L1: 0<s<dim_H(A), M002 with nonnegative exponent a=s gives μH[s](A)=infinity, hence H^s(A)=infinity; discharge L1. Under L2: dim_H(A)<s, M003 gives μH[s](A)=0, hence H^s(A)=0; discharge L2. Under L3: H^s(A)=0, F001 makes μH[s](A)=0≠infinity, and M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s; discharge L3. Under L4: H^s(A)=infinity, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A); discharge L4. These are the complete conditional assertions F002.

produces.statement: If 0<s<dim_H(A), H^s(A)=infinity; if dim_H(A)<s, H^s(A)=0; if H^s(A)=0, dim_H(A)≤s; if H^s(A)=infinity, dim_H(A)≥s.

argument.text: By H003, E is compact, hence bounded in its Euclidean metric. A bounded subset of R^n is contained in a coordinate box [-b,b]^n for some b>0: each coordinate distance is at most the Euclidean distance, and increasing a bound if necessary makes it positive. This also holds in R^0. Record F001. H001 specifies the nonnegative ambient dimension; N001 gives D≥0.

produces.statement: There exists a positive real b with E⊆[-b,b]^n.

argument.text: Choose b from F001 and define C as declared. Under L1: n>0, fix arbitrary a and h under L2: a>n and L3: 0<h≤1. Divide each coordinate interval [-b,b] into ceil(2b/h) intervals of side at most h. Their number is at most (2b+1)/h in each coordinate, hence the resulting at most C h^(-n) closed cubes cover E. Each cube has Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n)h. Therefore their total a-cost is at most C h^(-n)(sqrt(n)h)^a=C n^(a/2)h^(a-n). Since a-n>0, this tends to zero as h decreases to zero, and their diameters also tend to zero. In particular, at each fixed target scale arbitrarily small h provides admissible covers with costs tending to zero, so H^a(E)=0. Discharge L3 after using the arbitrary mesh sizes. N001 with A=E, exponent a gives D≤a. Since a>n was arbitrary, D≤n (if D>n, choose a strictly between n and D). Discharge L2 and L1. This proves F002.

produces.statement: If n>0, then D≤n.

argument.text: Under L4: n=0, Euclidean R^0 consists of its single empty-coordinate point. H002 implies E=R^0. A cover by that singleton has diameter and s-cost zero for every positive exponent s. Thus H^s(E)=0 for all s>0, and N001 gives D≤s for every s>0, whence D=0 using D≥0. Discharge L4. By H001 the alternatives n=0 and n>0 exhaust the ambient dimensions. F002 and this branch give 0≤D≤n, so D is finite, with the stated singleton conclusion when n=0.

produces.statement: 0≤D≤n, D is finite, and n=0 implies E=R^0 and D=0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary positive s and delta. The open balls of radius delta/2 centered at the points of E form an open cover. By H003 there is a finite subcover, and each such ball has diameter at most delta. Its finite number of members and finite diameters give a finite total s-cost. The defining infimum therefore gives H^s_delta(E)<infinity. Together with F003 this proves N002.

Countable subadditivity of Lebesgue measure and |I|=1 give 1≤sum_i |J_i|≤sum_i rho_i+epsilon, using sum_{i≥0}2^(-i-1)=1. If sum_i rho_i is infinite the required inequality is immediate; if finite, letting the arbitrary epsilon decrease to zero yields F002: sum_i rho_i≥1. All sets measured here are open intervals or I, so no measurability of V_i is assumed.

argument.text: Under L1: n=0, N002 gives E=R^0 and D=0. The coordinate map from I to F obtained by adjoining the unique R^0 coordinate preserves all distances. Push forward the interval covers that give H^a(I)=0 for a>1 in N003; their diameters are unchanged, so H^a(F)=0 for all a>1. N001 gives dim_H(F)≤a for every a>1 and hence dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. argument.text: For the other branch introduce L2: n≥1. Fix arbitrary q under L3: q>D, and arbitrary positive delta and epsilon. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. Define r=min(1,delta/sqrt(2))>0; thus r≤1 and sqrt(2)r≤delta. By N001 applied to E, H^q(E)=0. The nonnegative content H^q_r(E) is at most this supremum, hence zero. The infimum defining that content therefore supplies a countable r-cover W with total q-cost<epsilon/2. Such covers exist, for example by the finite-ball-cover assertion in N002. This is the existence statement F001, before choosing W.

produces.statement: There exists a sequence W of subsets of R^n covering E, with diam(W_i)≤r for all i and sum_i diam(W_i)^q<epsilon/2.

argument.text: Choose W from F001. Define beta,U,K,r_i as declared. A nonempty zero-diameter Euclidean set is a singleton. Because n≥1, its replacement open ball has positive diameter beta_i≤r and q-cost beta_i^q≤epsilon*2^(-i-3)<epsilon*2^(-i-2). Nonempty positive-diameter members are unchanged; every point originally covered remains covered. The additional cost is at most sum_{i≥0}epsilon*2^(-i-3)=epsilon/4<epsilon/2. Thus, after discarding empty members by restricting to K, U is a countable cover of E with 0<r_i≤r and sum_{i∈K}r_i^q<epsilon. This is F002; the countable index set may be finite.

produces.statement: The family (U_i)_(i∈K) covers E, 0<r_i≤r≤1 for i∈K, r_i=diam(U_i), and sum_(i∈K)r_i^q<epsilon.

argument.text:
For i∈K define N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Divide I into N_i closed intervals, each of length 1/N_i≤r_i. Since r_i≤1, N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F. The Euclidean distance formula in D006 shows that every product member has diameter at most sqrt(2)r_i≤sqrt(2)r≤delta. Their total (q+1)-cost is bounded by
sum_(i∈K) N_i (sqrt(2)r_i)^(q+1)
≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) sum_(i∈K) r_i^q
<2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.
These inequalities follow termwise from N_i≤2/r_i and then by nonnegative summation, so they remain valid for countably many members. Consequently H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon, which is F003.

produces.statement: H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.

argument.text: For fixed q and delta, epsilon>0 was arbitrary; the content in F003 is independent of epsilon, so it is zero. Since delta>0 was arbitrary, H^(q+1)(F)=0. N001, with ambient dimension n+1 and positive exponent q+1, gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since q>D was arbitrary and D is finite by N002, let q decrease to D to obtain dim_H(F)≤D+1: an alleged strict excess would allow a q between D and dim_H(F)-1, contradicting this bound (an infinite dimension is already excluded by any one q>D). Discharge L3 and L2. This proves F004.

produces.statement: If n≥1, dim_H(F)≤D+1.

argument.text: A natural dimension n is either zero or at least one. F000 and F004 thus give dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. By N002 the right hand side is finite, proving the finiteness clause as well.

argument.text: Define the nonnegative functions f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t). They are measurable because each J_i is open and each coefficient is a fixed finite nonnegative real. original_context.full_target:
# Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.

original_context.full_target:
# Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.

Borel measurability implies μ-almost-everywhere measurability for each summand. Monotonicity of the nonnegative integral and the integral of a constant on a set of measure one give
c≤∫_I sum_i f_i(t) dλ
 =sum_i ∫_I f_i(t) dλ

 ≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+sum_i eta_i rho_i^s

For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

# Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
